title: Quality register and product register
blurb: Tell the quality register from the product register by purpose and contents, and pick the right one for a status or results question.
question: The project manager wants to see which of the stage's products are approved, accepted or still in progress. Which register should she check?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile keeps both quality practice registers. The quality register summarizes all quality management activities that are planned or have taken place. The product register lists all products required by a plan and the status of each one. One answers 'what checks have we planned and what were the results?'; the other answers 'which products exist and where has each one got to?'.

root.label: What do you need to know?

teach.body: In managing product delivery, executing a work package includes notifying the project manager of completed quality activities and products and obtaining approvals for completed products. Evaluating a work package includes reviewing registers and logs and updating the team dashboard, so the project manager can pull current information. The registers stay; agile simply keeps them up to date in short cycles.

Ashgrove Construction is producing a digital site-induction pack: six videos, a quiz and a handbook. Project manager Sian Pritchard is asked which items are approved and which are still being built: she checks the product register, which shows two approved, one accepted and four in progress. Project assurance asks whether the quiz passed its accessibility review: that answer, with the method, dates and result, is in the quality register.

teach.text: STATUS of products is in the PRODUCT register. The quality register shows quality activities and their pass or fail results. A passed check does not tell you a product is complete or accepted, and a list of products does not tell you which checks passed.

teach.h: Not the only place information lives
teach.body: Do not confuse the registers with other quality and progress artifacts. The quality management approach describes how quality will be achieved, not individual results. The team dashboard shows team progress and replaces the checkpoint report. The product backlog holds user stories with acceptance criteria. Each register keeps a single, simple record that others can rely on.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 9.1, Table 12.1

items: Quality register: all quality management activities planned or done (Table 9.1).
Quality register fields: identifiers, quality method, planned and actual dates, responsibilities, pass or fail result, records.
Product register: all products required by a plan and their status.
Product register fields: product identifier, approval and acceptance dates, status, references.
Status question: product register. Results of checks: quality register.
Teams review registers and logs when evaluating a work package (Table 13.12).

summary: You can now tell the quality register (quality activities, dates and pass or fail results) from the product register (products and their status). You can also choose the right one for a question about results or about product status.

A.q: What does the product register contain?
options: All quality activities planned or carried out
All products required by a plan and their status
All risks to the products with their owners
All requests to change products in the baseline
A.why: The product register lists all products required of a plan and the status of those products (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: Planned and completed quality activities are summarized in the quality register.
whyNot.2: Risks and their owners are recorded in the risk register.
whyNot.3: Requests for change are issues, recorded in the issue register.

A.q: What does the quality register summarize?
options: The products in a plan and their approval status
The quality techniques and standards to be applied
The users' acceptance criteria for the project product
The quality activities planned or having taken place
A.why: The quality register summarizes all quality management activities that are planned or have occurred (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: Products and their status are in the product register.
whyNot.1: Techniques and standards are described in the quality management approach.
whyNot.2: Acceptance criteria for the project product are held with the project backlog.

A.q: Which item would you expect to find in the quality register?
options: The pass or fail result of a review
The current status of each product
The date the board approved the PID
The priority of each user story
A.why: Quality register entries include the quality method, planned and actual dates, responsibilities and the result, pass or fail (Table 9.1).

whyNot.1: Product status is recorded in the product register.
whyNot.2: PID approval is a board decision in directing a project, not a quality register entry.
whyNot.3: Story priority is held in the product backlog.

B.q: A board member asks which deliverables in the current stage have been approved, which accepted and which are not yet complete. Which product gives this?
B.why: The product register lists all products required of a plan with approval and acceptance dates and the status of each (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: The quality register shows quality activities and results, not each product's status.
whyNot.1: The quality management approach describes how quality will be achieved.
whyNot.3: The lessons log records lessons for this or future projects.

B.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. The [?] records the quality method, planned and actual dates, responsibilities and the pass or fail result of each quality activity.
B.why: These are the contents of the quality register (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: The product register holds the product identifier, approval and acceptance dates, status and references.
whyNot.2: The issue register records issues, not quality activities.
whyNot.3: The team dashboard shows team progress and replaces the checkpoint report.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. The product register includes approval and acceptance dates.
2. The quality register records the status of every product.
3. The quality register includes the quality method used.
4. The product register records each review's pass or fail result.
B.why: The product register includes approval and acceptance dates (1), and the quality register includes the quality method (3) (Table 9.1).

whyNot.1: Statement 2 is wrong: product status is in the product register.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: status is in the product register and pass or fail results are in the quality register.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: pass or fail results are in the quality register.

C.q: All planned reviews in a stage show 'pass', but some products are not yet finished. Which register shows the reviews, and which shows that products are unfinished?
C.why: Review results are in the quality register; the status of each product, including unfinished ones, is in the product register (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: This reverses them: reviews are in the quality register and status in the product register.
whyNot.1: The issue register records issues, not product status.
whyNot.3: The issue register records issues, not review results.

C.q: In managing product delivery, which activity includes reviewing registers and logs, and which artifact does the team then update?
options: Accept a work package; the release map
Notify work package completion; the project dashboard
Execute a work package; the product backlog
Evaluate a work package; the team dashboard
C.why: Evaluating a work package includes reviewing registers and logs and updating the team dashboard so the project manager can pull information (Table 13.12).

whyNot.0: Accepting a work package produces a team plan; the release map is updated by the project manager.
whyNot.1: Notifying completion tells the PM the work package is done; the project dashboard is for the board.
whyNot.2: Executing a work package is doing the work and reporting completed quality activities.

C.q: A tester's accessibility review of a booking screen has just finished with a 'fail'. Where is the result recorded, and what does the product register still show for the screen?
options: Quality register; the screen is not yet approved
Product register; the screen is closed as rejected
Issue register; the screen is moved to the backlog
Quality register; the screen is accepted by users
C.why: The review and its fail result go in the quality register; the product register keeps the screen's status, which cannot be approved while it has failed its review (Table 9.1, 9.3.2.2).

whyNot.1: Review results belong in the quality register, not the product register.
whyNot.2: A failed review is a quality result, not an issue for the issue register.
whyNot.3: A product that has failed its review is not done, so it cannot be accepted.

reteach.title: The exam board and the class list
reteach.question: How do you keep the two registers apart under exam pressure?

blocks.body: A school keeps a results sheet: each test sat, its date, who marked it and the grade. That is the quality register. It also keeps a class list: every pupil and whether they are enrolled, graduated or still studying. That is the product register. Asking 'who has graduated?' needs the class list, even if every test result looks fine.

blocks.text: The word 'status' in a question points to the product register. The words 'method', 'review result' or 'pass or fail' point to the quality register.

explain.body: Summarizes all quality management activities that are planned or have taken place, with their methods, dates, responsibilities and pass or fail results.

test.q: Where would a planned peer review of a training video be logged?
test.why: Planned and completed quality activities are summarized in the quality register (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: The product register lists products and their status, not quality activities.
whyNot.3: The daily log records informal issues, actions and events.

explain.body: Lists all products required by a plan with the product identifier, approval and acceptance dates, current status and references.

test.q: Which register would show that the handbook was accepted on 12 June?
test.why: The product register records approval and acceptance dates and the status of each product (Table 9.1).

whyNot.0: The quality register records quality activities and results.

explain.body: Status questions go to the product register. Questions about whether checks were carried out and passed go to the quality register.

test.q: Assurance asks whether every planned quality review this stage has taken place. Which product answers this?
test.why: The quality register shows planned and actual dates of quality activities, so it reveals whether planned reviews took place (Table 9.1).

whyNot.1: The product register shows product status, not whether each review happened.
whyNot.2: The project dashboard summarizes project progress for the board.
whyNot.3: The release map plans releases and iterations.

explain.body: When a work package is evaluated, the team reviews registers and logs and updates the team dashboard, so the project manager can pull up-to-date information.

test.q: Which activity in managing product delivery includes reviewing registers and logs?
test.why: Evaluating a work package includes reviewing registers and logs and updating the team dashboard (Table 13.12).

whyNot.0: Accepting a work package means reviewing the user stories and producing a team plan.
whyNot.1: Notifying completion tells the PM the work package is complete.
whyNot.2: Authorizing a work package is a controlling a stage activity for the PM.
